title: Tiered Routing 'BatchLock' Safeguard: automated recommendations + safe apply/rollback
creator: Priya Patel
description: Implement a per-customer and per-route recommendation engine (BatchLock) that proposes batching and KV-cache configurations based on traffic segmentation and tiering, plus an automated safe-apply workflow with canary rollout and immediate rollback triggers. The goal is to reduce per-token cost across customers while ensuring latency SLOs are preserved and high-value customers are not adversely impacted. Deliverables include: recommendation generator, validation heuristics, canary/rollback orchestration, UI surface in Console for review/approve, and audit logs for compliance.
acceptance_criteria: Recommendation generator produces candidate batching/cache configs per route and per-customer with confidence scores and estimated cost delta
Automated validation simulates latency impact on synthetic traces and rejects proposals exceeding configured risk thresholds
Safe-apply pipeline supports canary when applying to 1% -> 10% -> 100% traffic with health gates (p50/p95 latency, error rate, token throughput)
Rollback triggers automatically on gate failures and revert is observable in Console within 30s of trigger
Audit log entries created for each proposal, approval, apply step, and rollback with operator and commit info
Console shows per-route before/after cost estimate and allows manual override/whitelist of customers
test_plan: Unit tests for recommendation heuristics (edge cases: low-volume customers, bursty routes)
Integration test: deploy canary changes in staging cluster that mimics 3 traffic profiles (low, medium, high) and assert health gates
Load test: run mixed-sequence workloads to validate KV cache hit stabilization and observed cost reduction
Chaos test: simulate node failover during canary to confirm rollback path and observability
E2E: Console approve/apply/rollback flows with audit verification
rollout_plan: Phase 0 - internal QA: run recommendations across sample of internal customers and verify simulated metrics
Phase 1 - opt-in partners: enable for 5 pilot customers (diverse tiers) with manual approval required
Phase 2 - automated canary: auto-apply to 1% routed traffic for 24h, monitor gates, then 10% for 6h
Phase 3 - global: expand to all routes with customer-tier guardrails and allowlist exemptions
rollback_plan: Immediate automatic rollback when any canary gate exceeds threshold (configurable per route)
Operator manual rollback: Console button to revert to previous config with single click and linked PR
Fallback model variant: if batch/config change causes QoS regression, traffic automatically falls back to pinned model variant for 10 minutes while rollback completes
Post-rollback analysis: collect traces and generate incident ticket with root-cause hypothesis
notes: Trade-offs: aggressive batching reduces cost but may increase p95 for short requests. We prefer conservative batching for low-latency routes and allow heavier batching on background/embedding routes.
Whitelist semantics: explicit allowlist of customers prevents any automated apply; denylist prevents recommendations but allows operator manual changes.
Segmentation: use existing segmentation signals (customer-tier, route-category, sequence-length-percentile) and add a traffic-stability score to filter noisy candidates.
Cost estimation: we compute estimated token-cost delta with historical baseline and simulated batching gains; add confidence bands to avoid overpromising.
Security/compliance: all auto-applies log KMS key id and operator context for audit. No changes to private deployments without customer opt-in.
